source.title: Group actions on 1-manifolds: a list of very concrete open questions

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a lattice in a higher-rank simple Lie group that admits a nontrivial action by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of the interval?

evidence.quote: Question 1. Does there exist a lattice in a higher-rank simple Lie group admitting a nontrivial action by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of the interval ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an infinite finitely generated Kazhdan group that embeds in the group of homeomorphisms of the circle?

evidence.quote: Question 2. Does there exist an infinite, finitely-generated Kazhdan group of circle homeomorphisms ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a nontrivial Kazhdan group, and therefore an infinite one, that acts by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of the interval?

evidence.quote: Question 3. Does there exist a nontrivial (hence infinite) Kazhdan group of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of the interval ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an infinite finitely generated group with the following property: every action of the group on the real line by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms and without global fixed points is of type (iii), meaning that it is semiconjugate to a minimal action for which every bounded interval can be contracted along suitable group elements?

evidence.quote: (iii) The action is semiconjugate to a minimal one for which the contraction property above holds for all bounded intervals.

Question 4. Does there exist an infinite, finitely-generated group that acts on the real line all of whose actions by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of the line without global fixed points are of type (iii) ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a finitely generated amenable left-orderable group whose space of left orders is infinite but contains at least one isolated left order?
accepted.context_brief: Isolated left orders in amenable groups

evidence.quote: Question 5. Does there exist a finitely-generated, amenable, left-orderable group having an isolated order inside an infinite space of left orders ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a finitely generated left-orderable group for which the conjugation action on the space of all left orders is minimal, that is, every orbit of a left order under conjugation is dense?
accepted.context_brief: Minimal conjugacy action on left orders

evidence.quote: Question 6. Does there exist a finitely-generated, left-orderable group for which the conjugacy action on its space of left orders is minimal (that is, all the orbits are dense) ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a finitely generated left-orderable group that has no free subgroup and admits no nontrivial homomorphism to the integers?

evidence.quote: Question 7. Does there exist a finitely-generated, left-orderable group without free subgroups and admitting no nontrivial homomorphism into Z ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a finitely generated left-orderable group G such that G has no nontrivial homomorphism to the integers and its second bounded cohomology group H_b^2(G, R) is trivial?

evidence.quote: Question 8. Does there exist a finitely-generated, left-orderable group G with no nontrivial homomorphism into Z and trivial group of bounded cohomology H2_b(G, R) ?

accepted.question_text: Is the group of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of the closed 2-disk that restrict to the identity on the boundary left-orderable?

evidence.quote: Question 9. Is the group of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms of the 2-disk that are the identity at the boundary left orderable ?

accepted.question_text: Is Thompson’s group F amenable?

evidence.quote: Question 10. Is Thompson’s group F amenable ?

accepted.question_text: Does the group of piecewise-affine homeomorphisms of the circle contain any distorted element, meaning an element of infinite order whose word length grows sublinearly in its iterates inside some finitely generated subgroup?

evidence.quote: An element of infinite order g ∈ G is said to be distorted if limn→∞ ||g^n||/n = 0.
Question 11. Does the group of piecewise-affine circle homeomorphisms contain distorted elements ?

accepted.question_text: Which groups of piecewise-projective homeomorphisms of the interval or the circle are topologically conjugate to groups of C^1 diffeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Question 12. What are the groups of piecewise-projective homeomorphisms of the interval/circle that are topologically conjugate to groups of C1 diffeomorphisms ?

accepted.question_text: Given real numbers 0 < α < β < 1, does there exist a finitely generated group of C^{1+α} diffeomorphisms of the circle or interval that does not embed into the group of C^{1+β} diffeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Question 13. Given 0 < α < β < 1, does there exist a finitely-generated group of C1+α diffeomorphisms of the circle/interval that does not embed into the group of C1+β diffeomorphisms ?
Added in Proof. Question 13 has been recently solved by Kim and Koberda in a new version of [80].

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finitely generated group of C^2 circle diffeomorphisms, and assume that G has an exceptional minimal set Λ, meaning a minimal invariant Cantor set. Must the Lebesgue measure of Λ be zero?

evidence.quote: Question 14. Let G be a finitely-generated group of C2 circle diffeomorphisms. Assume that G admits an exceptional minimal set Λ. Is the Lebesgue measure of Λ equal to zero ?

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finitely generated group of C^2 circle diffeomorphisms with an exceptional minimal set Λ. Is the set of G-orbits of connected components of S^1 \ Λ finite?

evidence.quote: Question 15. Let G be a finitely-generated group of C2 circle diffeomorphisms. Assume that G admits an exceptional minimal set Λ. Is the set of orbits of intervals of S1 \ Λ finite ?

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finitely generated group of C^2 circle diffeomorphisms with an exceptional minimal set Λ. Is the action of G restricted to Λ topologically conjugate to the action of some group of piecewise-affine homeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Question 16. Let G be a finitely-generated group of C2 circle diffeomorphisms. Assume that G admits an exceptional minimal set Λ. Is the restriction of the action of G to Λ topologically conjugated to the action of a group of piecewise-affine homeomorphisms ?

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finitely generated group of C^2 circle diffeomorphisms. If the action of G on the circle is minimal, must it be ergodic with respect to Lebesgue measure?

evidence.quote: Question 17. Let G be a finitely-generated group of C2 circle diffeomorphisms. If the action of G is minimal, is it necessarily ergodic with respect to the Lebesgue measure ?

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finitely generated group of C^2 orientation-preserving circle diffeomorphisms. Does there exist a non-degenerate probability distribution on G, meaning one whose support generates G as a semigroup, such that the associated stationary measure on the circle is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure?

evidence.quote: a probability measure µ on M is said to be stationnary with respecto to p if for every measurable subset A⊂M, one has µ(A) = Σ_g∈G p(g)µ(g^{-1}(A)).

Question 18. Let G be a finitely-generated group of C2 orientation-preserving circle diffeomorphisms. Does there exist a non-degenerate probability distribution on G for which the stationary measure is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure ?

accepted.question_text: Fix a symmetric, finitely supported, non-degenerate probability distribution on Thompson’s group T. Is the Poisson-Furstenberg boundary of T for that random walk measurable-isomorphic to the circle equipped with the corresponding stationary measure?

evidence.quote: Question 19. Given a symmetric, finitely-supported, non-degenerate probability distribution on Thompson’s group T, does the Poisson-Furstenberg boundary of T with respect to it identifies with the circle endowed with the corresponding stationary measure ?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a faithful action of the free abelian group Z^2 on the circle by orientation-preserving C^∞ diffeomorphisms that is C^∞ structurally stable?

evidence.quote: Question 20. Does there exist a faithful action of Z2 by C∞ orientation-preserving circle diffeomorphisms that is C∞ structurally stable ?

accepted.question_text: For each r ≥ 1, is the subspace of (Diff^r_+(S^1))^2 consisting of commuting pairs of orientation-preserving C^r circle diffeomorphisms locally connected?

evidence.quote: Question 21. Given r ≥ 1, is the subset of Diff^r_+(S1)^2 consisting of pairs of commuting diffeomorphisms locally connected ?

accepted.question_text: Let φ₀ be a faithful action of a finitely generated group G on the circle by C^∞ diffeomorphisms, and assume that φ₀ admits an exceptional minimal set. Does there exist a path (φ_t)_{t∈[0,1]} of faithful actions, continuous in the C^∞ topology, such that φ_t has an exceptional minimal set for every t < 1 and φ_1 is minimal?
accepted.context_brief: Deforming exceptional actions to minimal ones

evidence.quote: Question 22. Given a faithful action φ0 of a finitely generated group G by C∞ circle diffeomorphisms admitting an exceptional minimal set, does there exist a path φt of faithful actions of G that is continuous in the C∞ topology and starts with φ0 = φ so that each φt admits an exceptional minimal set for t < 1 and φ1 is minimal ?

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finitely generated group of circle homeomorphisms whose action is C^0 structurally stable, and suppose that G admits infinitely many pairwise non-semi-conjugate actions on the circle. Must G contain a free subgroup on two generators?

evidence.quote: Question 23. Let G be a finitely-generated group of circle homeomorphisms whose action is C0 structurally stable. Suppose that G admits infinitely many non semiconjugate actions on the circle. Does G contain a free subgroup in two generators ?

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finitely generated group of C^1 circle diffeomorphisms with no resilient pairs, where a resilient pair means points x < y and elements f, g with x < f(x) < f(y) < g(x) < g(y) < y. For every ε > 0, can one conjugate G by a homeomorphism to a group of Lipschitz homeomorphisms whose chosen generators all have Lipschitz constant at most e^ε?

evidence.quote: there are no elements f, g such that x < f(x) < f(y) < g(x) < g(y) < y for certain points x, y.

Question 24. Let G be a finitely-generated group of C1 circle diffeomorphisms. Suppose that G has no resilient pairs. Given ε > 0, can G be conjugated (by a homeomorphism) into a group of Lipschitz homeomorphisms for which the Lipschitz constants of the generators are all ≤ e^ε ?

accepted.question_text: Let f be a C^2 circle diffeomorphism with irrational rotation number ρ. Is the rotation R_ρ contained in the C^2-closure of the set of all C^2 conjugates of f?

evidence.quote: Question 25. Let f be a C2 circle diffeomorphism of irrational rotation number ρ. Does the set of C2 conjugates of f contain the rotation Rρ in its C2-closure ?

accepted.question_text: For which real numbers r > 1 does there exist s ≥ r such that, for every C^s circle diffeomorphism f with irrational rotation number ρ, the sequence f^{q_n} converges to the identity in the C^r topology, where q_n denotes the denominators of the rational approximations of ρ?

evidence.quote: Question 26. For which values of r > 1 there exists s ≥ r such that for every Cs circle diffeomorphism f of irrational rotation number ρ, the sequence f^{qn} converges to the identity in the Cr topology, where (qn) is the sequence of denominators of the rational approximations of ρ ?

accepted.question_text: Let f be a C^2 circle diffeomorphism with irrational rotation number ρ. For ε > 0, form the mapping torus M_ε by identifying (x, 0) with (f(x), ε) in S^1 × [0, ε], and let ρ(ε) ∈ R/Z be the parameter for which M_ε corresponds to the elliptic curve C/(Z + iρ(ε)Z). Does ρ(ε) converge to ρ as ε tends to 0?

evidence.quote: Question 27. Let f be a C2 circle diffeomorphism of irrational rotation number ρ. Given ε > 0, let Mε be the mapping torus of f over S1 × [0, ε], that is, the surface obtained by identifying (x, 0) ∼ (f(x), ε). Let ρ(ε) ∈ R/Z be such that Mε corresponds to the elliptic curve C/(Z+iρ(ε)Z). Does ρ(ε) converges to ρ as ε → 0 ?

accepted.question_text: For groups of C^2 circle diffeomorphisms, is the restriction of the Godbillon-Vey cohomology class invariant under topological conjugacy?

evidence.quote: Question 28. Is the (restriction of the) Godbillon-Vey class invariant under topological conjugacy for groups of C2 diffeomorphisms ?

accepted.question_text: Which minimally acting groups of C^2 circle diffeomorphisms have the property that their normalizer inside the group of absolutely continuous homeomorphisms is exactly the same as their normalizer inside the group of diffeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Question 29. What are the groups of C2 circle diffeomorphisms acting minimally for which the normalizer inside the group of absolutely continuous homeomorphisms coincides with that inside the group of diffeomorphisms ?

accepted.question_text: Does Denjoy’s theorem remain true for circle homeomorphisms whose graphs are real-analytic, even when singularities may also occur for the inverse map?

evidence.quote: Question 30. Does Denjoy’s theorem hold for circle homeomorphisms whose graphs are real-analytic ?

accepted.question_text: Is the continuous cohomology of the group Diff^ω_+(S^1) of orientation-preserving real-analytic circle diffeomorphisms generated by the Euler class and the Godbillon-Vey class?

evidence.quote: Question 31. Is the continuous cohomology of the group Diff^ω_+(S1) of orientation-preserving, real-analytic circle diffeomorphisms generated by the Euler and the Godbillon–Vey classes ?

accepted.question_text: Is the group of orientation-preserving C^2 diffeomorphisms of the circle simple?

evidence.quote: Question 32. Is the group of orientation-preserving C2 circle diffeomorphisms simple ?

accepted.question_text: Does the Tits alternative hold for Diff^ω_+(S^1)? More concretely, must every non-metabelian subgroup of the group of orientation-preserving real-analytic circle diffeomorphisms contain a free subgroup?
accepted.context_brief: Tits alternative for real-analytic circle groups

evidence.quote: Question 33. Does the Tits alternative hold in Diffω_+(S1) ? More precisely, does every non-metabelian subgroup of this group contain a free subgroup ?

trace.notes: Resolved the arXiv abs URL to a local PDF copy and mapped sections 1-11 plus the Added in Proof note. Open-question regions were located on pages 3-16.
Extracted all 33 explicitly numbered Question blocks from the PDF and retained the Added in Proof note because it explicitly marks Question 13 as solved.

Rewrote each numbered question into standalone form, expanding source-specific shorthand such as type (iii), resilient pairs, stationary measures, and exceptional minimal sets only when supported by nearby source text.
No near-duplicate question statements were merged; the paper presents 33 distinct numbered questions.

All accepted items have verbatim evidence with page locators and were checked for unsupported cross-references. Question 13 was marked solved because the same source explicitly says it was solved in the Added in Proof note.
Saved exact JSON to outputs/parse-paper/1712.06462.json and updated outputs/latest.json.
